pr_title: Keep property values when extending script
pr_body:
Closes #37480
EDIT: Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4415

~~This can also trigger when replacing a script for one node. Making it work only with script extending would make the code more complicated, because the editor doesn't really differentiate between extending and attaching. I don't think this is a big issue.~~

I added 2 methods in EditorNode:
`store_object_properties()` and `apply_object_properties()`. The first one gets properties from the script instance and stores it in EditorNode, the second one applies it to the new instance, to the properties that have matching name and type. The intended usage is that you call these methods as part of a UndoRedo action that changes script and the exported values are carried to the new script.

The values will be preserved when:
- extending script
- making script unique
- attaching a new script
- if you know any other action that can potentially clear exported variables, please comment
pr_comments:
I rebased and improved the PR.

Aside from extending script, the properties will now be kept when making the script unique or attaching a new one (regardless if it's the same script or a completely different one; properties with the same name will keep values).
@reduz suggests that @vnen should review this. Ideally this should/could be fixed in the script itself so that this workaround is not necessary in the editor.

Not sure how can this be fixed in script if the script is replaced by a different one. This is editor issue, because the script is removed and a new one is added and only editor can keep track of the former variables.

issue_context.title: Extending a GDScript on a node clears the exported script variables.
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** 3.2.1 / master (a2da99f40cf2123c0906c734a2eb01e9b65a45a2)

**OS/device including version:** Windows 10

**Issue description:**
Using Extend Script on a node with an attached script (notably scripts with `class_name`s and hence appearing as types in Add Child dialogs) clears the existing script variables on the node.

**Steps to reproduce:**
* Provided Reproduction
  * Create a script with `class_name`s (`A`).
  * Create a new node with with the type
* Extend the node with the attached script.

**Minimal reproduction project:** [TempTest.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4412229/TempTest.zip)
comments:
Related to #37479 

There is a common misbehavior around changing the type of nodes with GDScripts on them. Also notable are:

* Dropping a script that *extends* the script currently on a node clears the script variables.
* Dropping a script that *is a sibling* of the script currently on a node clears the script variables.
* Dropping a script that *is extended* by the script currently on a node clears the script variables.

All of which are situations I would expect to work correctly.
I would be willing to attempt fix these two issues and improve this overall (fixing the additional three cases above). I could also create a proposal for this behavior if necessary.

Upon implementing some code to (attempt a broken) fix for the issue in #37479 I realized the correct way to implement all of the above is probably with duck typing. As that is how the code appears to be written in the first place (these functions attempt to copy variables right now)! It just isn't working at the moment (for scripts at least).

So I guess the proposal/fix I might submit here is to call the "change type" code, which in turn calls the `Node::replace_by` code which copies variables (I am about to have a pull request to fix #37479 that improves the behavior of this code), instead of calling into the `Object::set_script` code directly. I have two reasons suggest this:

1. It will allow variables to propagate to the new script from the old script (via duck typing).
2. It will better support undo/redo (specifically it will store the variables of the script).

A downside of this is that we will end up creating a new node every time a script is changed from the editor. This also means that the script instance will not be modified and will instead continue to persist with the old node in the undo history (I don't know if there would be negative side effects to this). Also I suspect for heavier nodes (MeshInstance?) duplicating them a bunch (rather than just changing the script variable) could be considered excessive. However I would contend that changing which script is attached to which node is a relatively uncommon occurrence.

The better middle ground is probably adding a variant of (or flag to) `Object::set_script` that attempts to do a "duck typed" copy of the script parameters (similar to how the duplicate/change type code does it right now). I am not sure if this is actually easily possible though.

Again I am willing to implement this.
